analysis:
The supplied units are only CHANGELOG.md head text (lines 1572-2095); the file_changes patch shows an added release-notes section for v0.10.6. I found no executable code, config, or policy changes. The changelog is documentation only, so I identified no concrete security regression.

Security-relevant claims examined:
- Prefix cache (T-041): the notes say prefix reuse is partitioned by the authenticated cache scope. They also describe an opt-in Nemotron resident checkpoint bank and the GLM SSD prefix store, which is default-on for the pinned GLM identity, with DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 as the opt-out. They add that the DEBUG-only DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE path is not in release builds. These are consistent with the T-041 posture. They do not raise the TTL or weaken account isolation. The Nemotron resident bank and GLM SSD store use existing mechanisms, but their code was not supplied. Whether the GLM SSD per-donation gate and HMAC naming apply unchanged is unverified.
- The notes describe image and video ingress limits, such as PNG chunk limits, JPEG scan checks, frame and pixel caps, and a decoder time allowance. These are availability mitigations. The video decode path (T-050 class) states no temporary-file use. Its implementation was not supplied.
- Debug cache key file: described as DEBUG-only and absent from release builds. This is a build-gating claim I could not verify from the supplied text.
- Installer notes (relaxed signature check for -dev./-staging. versions, a staging lane and master-push publishing) are documentation of changes in other files not supplied. The relaxed check applies only to pre-release versions and keeps the bundle identifier pinned, but its implementation and the TB-013/T-061 interaction need review in scripts/install.sh and the workflows.
- Fan helper, watchdog and cluster notes (RDMA over Thunderbolt, cluster_runtime registration) describe changes that touch TB-010, T-043 and TB-002. Their implementations are outside the supplied evidence, and cluster trust-boundary handling is not covered by the current threat model.

Remaining questions for integration: the actual code behind the cluster, installer relaxation, debug cache key and prefix-cache scoping claims. I recommend a deeper review of the non-changelog files in this PR.
